scope: Reusable Java lifecycle/admission owner for synchronous effects invoked at their actual execution boundary. Not the provider loop, tool codec, session service or UI integration. Kotlin dispatch integration follows when the native driver exists; no coroutine wrapper is needed by this synchronous core.

requirements.statement: Only one run may own a lifecycle instance; a busy or closing/closed instance cannot admit another run.
Each batch is a nonempty immutable ordered collection of distinct nonblank CallIds; malformed batches fail construction before admission.
Only the next pending call in the current batch may start; at most one effect is executing. Another batch cannot replace an unsettled batch.

Stop and effect-start admission are linearized under the same monitor at execute entry inside the actual queued runnable. Stop winning prevents callback invocation. Admission winning counts as already started; no enqueue or suspension is allowed between admission and synchronous callback invocation.

Stop cancels every pending call, retains executing/completed dispositions, and blocks further effects and new runs. Already-started work may finish; finishRun requires a settled batch and explicit driver cleanup acknowledgement.

Each batch call has exactly one terminal status. Effect has no return value: normal return records COMPLETED; any Throwable, including a checked exception raised without a declaration, records FAILED_AFTER_START before rethrowing the same object. Lifecycle state retains only the status; no public complete method or automatic replay exists.

Run and batch handles are opaque identity capabilities; handles from another owner or previous generation cannot start, finish, stop, or overwrite current work. Lifecycle and batch snapshots contain no capability handles. Previously returned immutable snapshots remain readable; a stale handle cannot query a replaced batch.

close is idempotent: IDLE closes immediately; RUNNING or STOPPING enters CLOSING, cancels pending work and preserves an active run until finishRun acknowledges settlement; CLOSING and CLOSED never reopen.

Domain values, transitions and outcomes contain no PSI, JSON, coroutine, provider or unconstrained generic result objects. Effect is value-free and execution success is a closed variant. Expected rejection uses operation-local closed outcomes; programmer nulls fail before state mutation.
No monitor is held while an effect callback runs. Stop must return while a callback is blocked. State inspection returns immutable snapshots, never owner internals.

A RUNNING run can accept multiple settled batches and must have unique CallIds across that run. beginBatch validates every call and performs no mutation on rejection, including a mixed fresh/reused candidate. Stop/close cancel pending calls; unfinished batches cannot be silently discarded by finishRun.

Every stage is gated by canonical requirement and evidence IDs for exact frozen inputs. Each invariant has a type/API-first audit row, and each receipt binds stage, feature, spec/design/source hashes, configuration identity and evidence result hashes.

acceptance.when: Start twice; finish the first run; start again.
acceptance.then: Second start is BUSY; later start owns a new handle.

acceptance.when: Construct empty, duplicate-ID and null-containing batches; mutate the input list after valid construction.
acceptance.then: Invalid values rejected; admitted order unaffected by caller mutation.

acceptance.when: Attempt call B before A, call B while A is blocked, and execute A concurrently from two threads using barriers.
acceptance.then: B never invokes; exactly one A callback enters; the losing A attempt is ALREADY_EXECUTING; after A settles, B executes once and another A attempt is ALREADY_TERMINAL.

acceptance.when: Submit an effect invocation to an executor behind a gate; request Stop before releasing the gate.
acceptance.then: Callback counter remains zero; all pending calls are CANCELLED_BEFORE_START; no effect begins after Stop wins.

acceptance.when: Admit A, block inside its callback, then Stop and attempt finish/start; release A.
acceptance.then: Stop returns without callback release; no B runs; finish/start are rejected until A settles; A is COMPLETED or FAILED_AFTER_START; explicit finish releases the run.

acceptance.when: Execute value-free effects once with normal return, RuntimeException, AssertionError and a checked IOException thrown through a generic rethrow; attempt each again.
acceptance.then: One terminal status each; thrown object is rethrown unchanged after FAILED_AFTER_START accounting; no replay or nullable result exists.

acceptance.when: Use handles across owners and after starting a new generation; capture an old snapshot, replace the batch, then query with the old handle.
acceptance.then: No current state changes; captured snapshot remains readable and immutable; stale handle query returns STALE_BATCH and exposes no capability.

acceptance.when: Stop an active run, close it, close again, settle its active effect and acknowledge cleanup.
acceptance.then: Phase is STOPPING then CLOSING then CLOSED; pending calls cancel, active outcome is retained, close is idempotent, and start remains rejected forever.

acceptance.when: Inspect public signatures/dependencies and pass null to CallId, CallBatch.of, beginBatch, execute, stop, finishRun and batchSnapshot, recording snapshots before each mutating call.
acceptance.then: No forbidden dependency or generic effect result; each null fails before state mutation; no lifecycle or batch snapshot changes.

acceptance.when: Block callback; Stop and query from another thread; inspect earlier snapshot after later updates.
acceptance.then: Stop/query return without callback release; earlier snapshot is unchanged.

acceptance.when: Finish with calls pending; settle a batch; submit [freshB, reusedA]; then submit freshB in a new batch and finish normally.
acceptance.then: Pending finish rejects; mixed batch rejects without poisoning freshB; freshB later executes; normal finish transitions RUNNING to IDLE and a new run can start.

acceptance.when: Remove an audit binding and alter a frozen source hash in disposable copies.
acceptance.then: Bounded artifact/gate check rejects each; valid design shape alone does not mark behavior evidence passed.

acceptance.when: Run execute through the real AWT EventQueue behind a latch; exercise Stop-before-runnable and admission-before-Stop orderings separately.
acceptance.then: The first ordering invokes no callback; the second ordering records an executing callback and Stop returns without waiting; the owner cannot start another run until settlement.

type_safety_audit.invalid: Idle plus an active run, or two active runs
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Final RunLifecycle owner with private state and distinct final RunHandle; no public active-state constructor
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Synchronized startRun and owner-key identity checks serialize competing starts and reject foreign handles
type_safety_audit.justification: Java aliases do not enforce single ownership; no per-state wrapper is allowed to become stale authority

type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: CallId and private CallBatch factory; List.copyOf plus nonempty/distinct validation
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Constructor validation of externally supplied values
type_safety_audit.justification: Java has no built-in nonempty/unique list type; one domain wrapper is simpler than pervasive checks

type_safety_audit.invalid: Execute wrong call or two effects
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Private BatchState cursor/status map and no public completion mutator
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Cursor/admission checked under monitor on every attempt
type_safety_audit.justification: Sequential ordering involves changing shared state, not just a parameter type

type_safety_audit.invalid: Scheduled token grants effect after Stop
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: No public admission token; execute owns admission and immediate callback invocation
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Stop and execute share one monitor and linearization point
type_safety_audit.justification: No affine references or atomic world transition in Java; tests cover both race orderings

type_safety_audit.invalid: Stopping admits work or falsely claims rollback
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Stopping owns run state; finish returns Unsettled while work remains
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Driver invokes finish only after its own resources settle; this component accounts effects only
type_safety_audit.justification: Type state cannot force an external platform operation to terminate

type_safety_audit.invalid: Duplicate completion or contradictory outcome flags
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Value-free Effect; one terminal CallStatus; Executed and Rejected are disjoint closed variants; no public complete operation
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Normal return records COMPLETED; any Throwable records FAILED_AFTER_START and rethrows the same object; current executing identity is checked and terminal recording occurs once
type_safety_audit.justification: An effect failure is temporal/external and must be observed

type_safety_audit.invalid: CallId/RunHandle/BatchHandle mixup or forged public capability
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Distinct final handle types with package-private construction; LifecycleSnapshot and ordered BatchSnapshot contain no handles
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Private owner-key identity and current-handle checks reject foreign/replaced handles; captured snapshots are inert values
type_safety_audit.justification: Package-local construction alone cannot prove ownership or freshness

type_safety_audit.invalid: Closed with new admission or lost executing work
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: LifecyclePhase distinguishes STOPPING/CLOSING/CLOSED; close has no reopen transition
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: close cancels pending work; finish settles Closing
type_safety_audit.justification: External running effect can outlive content; no unconditional liveness claim

type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Value-free Effect, non-generic closed result algebras, ordered handle-free snapshots, no forbidden type imports, null-check constructors
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Null-check every public argument before state mutation; inspect public signatures/dependencies; no static whole-program nullness claim
type_safety_audit.justification: No JSpecify/NullAway requested; Java nullable references remain a stated limitation

type_safety_audit.invalid: Caller mutates internal state or Stop waits on arbitrary callback
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Immutable ordered snapshots; owner state, map and capability handles never exposed
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Release monitor before callback; capture snapshot under monitor
type_safety_audit.justification: Types do not prove lock duration or scheduling

type_safety_audit.invalid: Call IDs collide across accepted batches
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: CallBatch validates local uniqueness; run-private accepted ID set and atomic batch installation
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Reject reuse before admitting batch; finish requires settled state
type_safety_audit.justification: Identity uniqueness is relative to accumulated history

type_safety_audit.invalid: Green stage without concrete evidence or type audit
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Fixed requirement/audit/evidence/stage records and exact receipt identity fields
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Check referential coverage and hashes; reviewer judges prevention adequacy
type_safety_audit.justification: Structural checks cannot prove arbitrary semantic enforcement

non_goals: Actual PSI mutation algorithms, handles, rename and undo
Tool-window registration or UI callback delivery
assumptions: Caller constructs one lifecycle owner per native session; project service uniqueness is a later integration obligation.
Effect callbacks are synchronous; no work is queued or suspended after admission before the callback boundary.
The driver calls finishRun only after other owned resources settle. This component cannot discover detached work.
External callbacks eventually return if eventual settlement is claimed. Safety is required even when they do not.
